```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
```


```{r}
gl22 <- read.csv("Unnecessary Documents/gl2022.txt", header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

games22 <- gl22 %>%
  mutate(
    # Make sure V1 is character
    V1 = as.character(V1)
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Year = substr(V1, 1, 4),                     # first 4 chars = Year
    Date = as.Date(V1, format = "%Y%m%d"),       # convert yyyymmdd to Date
    Winning.Team = ifelse(as.integer(V10) > as.integer(V11), V4, V7),
    Losing.Team  = ifelse(as.integer(V10) > as.integer(V11), V7, V4),
    Winning.Score = pmax(as.integer(V10), as.integer(V11)),
    Losing.Score  = pmin(as.integer(V10), as.integer(V11)),
    Total.Score   = as.integer(V10) + as.integer(V11),
    Margin = as.integer(Winning.Score) - as.integer(Losing.Score)
  )

head(games22, 10)

# Save to a CSV
write.csv(games22, "Unnecessary Documents/mlb2022_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# 1) read in excel file
odds_22 <- read_excel("Unnecessary Documents/Oddsshark - 2022.xlsx")

# 2) Clean into a tidy O/U dataset
ou_lines <- odds_22 |>
  filter(!is.na(date), !is.na(`team 2`)) |>
  transmute(
    Date      = as.Date(date),
    Team      = `team 1`,
    Opponent0 = `team 2`,
# Home/Away based on the leading marker in Opponent0 ("vs" = home, "@" = away)
    HomeAway  = case_when(
      str_starts(Opponent0, "vs") ~ "Home",
      str_starts(Opponent0, "@")  ~ "Away",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Opponent  = str_remove(Opponent0, "^(vs|@)\\s*"),
    OU_Result = `O/U`,           # column with O/U result
    OU_Line   = as.numeric(`Lines`) # column with O/U line
  ) %>%
# Create explicit HomeTeam/AwayTeam
  mutate(
    HomeTeam = if_else(HomeAway == "Home", Team, Opponent),
    AwayTeam = if_else(HomeAway == "Home", Opponent, Team)
  ) %>%
# Keep only one row per game (home perspective)
  filter(HomeAway == "Home") %>%
  distinct(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam)

# 3) Check the result
head(ou_lines)

# 4) Save to CSV for joining with Retrosheet scores
write.csv(ou_lines, "Unnecessary Documents/OU_Lines_2022.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
# --- 1) Load your files ---
res <- read_csv("Unnecessary Documents/mlb2022_results.csv")   # Year, Date, Winning.Team, Losing.Team, ...
ou  <- read_csv("Unnecessary Documents/OU_Lines_2022.csv")     # Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, OU_Line, OU_Result, ...

# --- 2) Map OddsShark team names -> Retrosheet 3-letter codes ---
name_to_code <- c(
  "Arizona"="ARI","Atlanta"="ATL","Baltimore"="BAL","Boston"="BOS",
  "Chi Cubs"="CHN","Chi White Sox"="CHA","Cincinnati"="CIN","Cleveland"="CLE",
  "Colorado"="COL","Detroit"="DET","Houston"="HOU","Kansas City"="KCA",
  "LA Angels"="ANA","LA Dodgers"="LAN","Miami"="MIA","Milwaukee"="MIL",
  "Minnesota"="MIN","NY Mets"="NYN","NY Yankees"="NYA","Oakland"="OAK",
  "Philadelphia"="PHI","Pittsburgh"="PIT","San Diego"="SDN","San Francisco"="SFN",
  "Seattle"="SEA","St. Louis"="SLN","Tampa Bay"="TBA","Texas"="TEX",
  "Toronto"="TOR","Washington"="WAS"
)

# Ensure Date is Date type
res <- res %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
ou  <- ou  %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

# --- 3) Build an unordered "pair key" for both tables (so home/away doesn't matter) ---
# RESULTS: from winner/loser codes
res_keyed <- res %>%
  mutate(
    pair_codes = if_else(Winning.Team < Losing.Team,
                         paste(Winning.Team, Losing.Team, sep = "-"),
                         paste(Losing.Team, Winning.Team, sep = "-"))
  )

# OU LINES: map names to codes, then make the same unordered key
ou_keyed <- ou %>%
  mutate(
    HomeCode = name_to_code[HomeTeam],
    AwayCode = name_to_code[AwayTeam],
    pair_codes = if_else(HomeCode < AwayCode,
                         paste(HomeCode, AwayCode, sep = "-"),
                         paste(AwayCode, HomeCode, sep = "-"))
  )

# --- 4) Handle doubleheaders: add an occurrence index per (Date, pair) in each table ---
res_keyed <- res_keyed %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

ou_keyed <- ou_keyed %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- 5) Preserve original order of RESULTS ---
res_keyed <- res_keyed %>% mutate(row_id = row_number())

# --- 6) Join O/U onto RESULTS by Date + pair + occurrence ---
merged <- res_keyed %>%
  left_join(
    ou_keyed %>% select(Date, pair_codes, game_n, OU_Line, OU_Result,
                        HomeTeam, AwayTeam, HomeCode, AwayCode),
    by = c("Date","pair_codes","game_n")
  ) %>%
  arrange(row_id) %>%      # restore original order
  select(-row_id)

# --- 7) Save the merged file ---
write_csv(merged, "Unnecessary Documents/mlb2022_results_with_OU.csv")

```

```{r}
# --- files ---
res <- read_csv("Unnecessary Documents/mlb2022_results.csv")   # has Year/Date/Winner/Loser/Scores/Total.Score/Margin
ou  <- read_csv("Unnecessary Documents/OU_Lines_2022.csv")     # has Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, OU_Result (and maybe OU_Line)

# --- team name map: OddsShark -> Retrosheet codes ---
name_to_code <- c(
  "Arizona"="ARI","Atlanta"="ATL","Baltimore"="BAL","Boston"="BOS",
  "Chi Cubs"="CHN","Chicago Cubs"="CHN",
  "Chi White Sox"="CHA","Chicago White Sox"="CHA",
  "Cincinnati"="CIN","Cleveland"="CLE","Colorado"="COL","Detroit"="DET",
  "Houston"="HOU","Kansas City"="KCA",
  "LA Angels"="ANA","Los Angeles Angels"="ANA",
  "LA Dodgers"="LAN","Los Angeles Dodgers"="LAN",
  "Miami"="MIA","Milwaukee"="MIL","Minnesota"="MIN",
  "NY Mets"="NYN","New York Mets"="NYN",
  "NY Yankees"="NYA","New York Yankees"="NYA",
  "Oakland"="OAK","Philadelphia"="PHI","Pittsburgh"="PIT",
  "San Diego"="SDN","San Francisco"="SFN",
  "Seattle"="SEA","St. Louis"="SLN","Tampa Bay"="TBA",
  "Texas"="TEX","Toronto"="TOR","Washington"="WAS"
)

# ensure Date is Date
res <- res %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
ou  <- ou  %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

# --- unordered team-pair key (home/away agnostic) ---
res_keyed <- res %>%
  mutate(
    pair_codes = if_else(Winning.Team < Losing.Team,
                         paste(Winning.Team, Losing.Team, sep = "-"),
                         paste(Losing.Team, Winning.Team, sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%   # handles doubleheaders
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number())       # preserve original order

ou_keyed <- ou %>%
  mutate(
    HomeCode = name_to_code[HomeTeam],
    AwayCode = name_to_code[AwayTeam],
    pair_codes = if_else(HomeCode < AwayCode,
                         paste(HomeCode, AwayCode, sep = "-"),
                         paste(AwayCode, HomeCode, sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- join, restore order, and keep only requested columns ---
final <- res_keyed %>%
  left_join(
    ou_keyed %>% select(Date, pair_codes, game_n, OU_Result),
    by = c("Date","pair_codes","game_n")
  ) %>%
  arrange(row_id) %>%
  select(
    Year, Date,
    `Winning Team` = Winning.Team,
    `Losing Team`  = Losing.Team,
    `Winning Score`= Winning.Score,
    `Losing Score` = Losing.Score,
    `Total Score`  = Total.Score,
    Margin,
    `OU Result`    = OU_Result
  )

# write it out
write_csv(final, "Unnecessary Documents/mlb2022_results_with_OU_MINIMAL_RCODE.csv")

# quick sanity check
cat("Rows:", nrow(final), "\nMissing OU results:", sum(is.na(final$`OU Result`)), "\n")

```

```{r}
  "San Diego"="SDN","San Francisco"="SFN",
  "Seattle"="SEA","St. Louis"="SLN","Tampa Bay"="TBA",
  "Texas"="TEX","Toronto"="TOR","Washington"="WAS"
)

# ensure Date is Date
res <- res %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
ou  <- ou  %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

# --- unordered team-pair key (home/away agnostic) ---
res_keyed <- res %>%
  mutate(
    pair_codes = if_else(Winning.Team < Losing.Team,
                         paste(Winning.Team, Losing.Team, sep = "-"),
                         paste(Losing.Team, Winning.Team, sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%   # handles doubleheaders
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number())       # preserve original order

ou_keyed <- ou %>%
  mutate(
    HomeCode = name_to_code[HomeTeam],
    AwayCode = name_to_code[AwayTeam],
    pair_codes = if_else(HomeCode < AwayCode,
                         paste(HomeCode, AwayCode, sep = "-"),
                         paste(AwayCode, HomeCode, sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  group_by(Date, pair_codes) %>%
  mutate(game_n = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- join, restore order, and keep only requested columns ---
final <- res_keyed %>%
  left_join(
    ou_keyed %>% select(Date, pair_codes, game_n, OU_Result),
    by = c("Date","pair_codes","game_n")
  ) %>%
  arrange(row_id) %>%
  select(
    Year, Date,
    `Winning Team` = Winning.Team,
    `Losing Team`  = Losing.Team,
    `Winning Score`= Winning.Score,
    `Losing Score` = Losing.Score,
    `Total Score`  = Total.Score,
    Margin,
    `OU Result`    = OU_Result
  )

# write it out
write_csv(final, "Unnecessary Documents/mlb2024_results_with_OU_MINIMAL_RCODE.csv")

# quick sanity check
cat("Rows:", nrow(final), "\nMissing OU results:", sum(is.na(final$`OU Result`)), "\n")
```
